newsitem.title: GERMANY: INSTANT VIEW - German state June CPI data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - German state June CPI data.

text.p: Following are economists' reactions to June consumer price reports from the west German states of Bavaria and Baden-Wuerttemberg.
The statistics office in Bavaria reported on Monday that the cost of living there rose 0.2 percent from May and 1.6 percent from June 1996.
Baden-Wuerttemberg, said on Tuesday its consumer prices climbed 0.2 percent from the month before and 1.4 percent year-on-year.
HOLGER SCHMIEDING, ECONOMIST AT MERRILL LYNCH IN FRANKFURT.

"It is slightly worse than expected but not all that bad. petrol prices did not decline as much as we had been expecting so that is why the month/month rate has come in at 0.2 percent rather than 0.1 percent.
"But as we can see from the year/year rate, it continues to fluctuate around the 1.5 percent level, so there is no underlying inflation pressure.'
"This suggests that for west Germany as a whole we will see 0.2 percent month/month and 1.6 percent year/year."
ARMIN KAYSER, ECONOMIST AT SWISS BANK CORP IN FRANKFURT

"What is interesting is that we have seen prices accelerating at the intermediate level. Producer prices have been up from the very low levels seen last year. This is mainly related to the depreciation of the mark, which is feeding into prices. It could create an inflation hump over the next few months but it will not change the very favourable prospects for long-term price stability."
ADOLF ROSENSTOCK, ECONOMIST AT INDUSTRIAL BANK OF JAPAN IN FRANKFURT

"Its right in line with expectations. It matches our forecasts. The 0.2 percent is a reasonable figure. The uptick in yearly inflation should not be mistaken as a sign of higher underlying inflation. It is due to underlying reasons. We should now see 1.5 percent CPI later in the year. I would expect 0.2 percent and 1.6 percent for the preliminary west German report. The Bundesbank will not react to this at all. The last Bundesbank monthly report showed there are no inflation pressures in the economy."
